answer: Each agent identity must post a bond locked in a shared contract before it can submit work, and rewards accrue only after independent agents validate that work against a random challenge. The contract caps how many identities one funded account can activate at once, so splitting activity across quartz, opal, and vertex profiles does not multiply influence. A sybil attacker must tie up real capital for every identity and risks losing the bond when fabricated work fails validation; creating names is cheap, but sustaining trusted identities is not.
